gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-archivo: Noto Serif Hebrew leads with a literary, authoritative voice, its strokes shifting just enough to notice. Archivo follows in a sans with a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, giving the heading room to speak.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-fs-asap: Authoritative and literary, Noto Serif Hebrew carries a moderate contrast between stem and hairline. Asap slips in beneath it with open arcs and low contrast, and its body height nearly matches the capitals.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-fs-fira-sans: Glowing, tube-like lines make Fira Sans feel almost lit from within, against a heading that thins gently at its curves. And Noto Serif Hebrew keeps the top literary while the sans-serif body, with its large x-height, stays open and easy to follow.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-fs-public-sans: Slightly thinner joins where curves meet stems give Noto Serif Hebrew its quiet, literary character. But enlarge Public Sans, a hefty sans-serif with broad open counters, and it starts to crowd the heading's finer detail.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-fs-supreme: A mild thick-and-thin rhythm marks Noto Serif Hebrew as literary and authoritative. And Supreme, a crisp sans-serif with a heavy band of text and open letterforms, gives the pair its strongest quality: a firm weight difference.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-general-sans: Glass-rod strokes up top, a ribbon of constant width below. Noto Serif Hebrew is best at tapering, authoritative lettering, while General Sans does its best work with a smooth, steady sans line and an x-height that fills the line.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-manrope: Manrope reads bright and approachable, with a wide gap at every curve and a pen line holding one width. Manrope's plain sans uniformity sets off Noto Serif Hebrew, whose lighter horizontals are never threadlike, and that difference is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-montserrat: Montserrat is a geometric plain sans with generous white space before each curve and oversized e and a counters. And Noto Serif Hebrew, with its understated thick-thin contrast, adds a literary weight above that poured, single-width ink.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-satoshi: Satoshi, a sans with a soaring x-height and an open e that never squeezes shut, gives every stroke one width. Give it a little extra size under Noto Serif Hebrew.
gen-gf-noto-serif-hebrew-switzer: Noto Serif Hebrew writes like a brush under slight pressure, literary and authoritative with a stem-to-hairline ratio that stays moderate. Switzer answers with a blunt, marker-like sans, tubular and tall-waisted, and the pair's strongest quality is how clearly the two textures part ways.
